Q: Can´t undertand 10th line instruction after inner FOR loop A:

Instruction d[k] := 5 performs 3 functions:

  1. Note that d array is not initialized and will contain random values before the start of the loop. At the first iteration of the outer loop, the inner loop is skipped, and d array gets the starting value [5, ..].
  2. Each ith iteration requires calculating the expression 10*r + d[i] over elements 0..i inclusive. But for the last element to be calculated correctly, it is necessary that d[i] = 0. (But d array is not initialized!). Therefore, the inner loop ends ahead of schedule at position k-1. And the element d[k] is assigned a pre-known value of 5.
  3. The fact that instead of the instructions r := 10*r + d[i]; d[i] := r DIV 2 when i = k, the usual assignment d[k] := 5 is performed, this is a necessity, not an optimization.

Instruction Texts.Write(W, "5") just replaces a more cumbersome instruction: Texts.Write(W, CHR(d[k] + ORD("0"))).

If we do initialize the array, we will get rid of the last instructions d[k] := 5; Texts.Write(W, "5"), and we will also get a more universal algorithm for calculating fractions in any base (not just decimal ones):

PROCEDURE Power (VAR W: Texts.Writer; N, B: INTEGER);
  (* compute decimal representation of negative powers of 2 *)
VAR i, k, r: INTEGER;
    d: ARRAY N OF INTEGER;
    p, s: REAL; (* for verification *)
BEGIN
  (* initialization *)
  d[0] := B; FOR k := 1 TO N-1 DO d[k] := 0 END;

  FOR k := 0 TO N-1 DO
    Texts.Write(W, "."); r := 0;
    FOR i := 0 TO N-1 DO
      r := B*r + d[i]; d[i] := r DIV 2; r := r MOD 2;
      Texts.Write(W, CHR(d[i] + ORD("0")))
    END;

    (* reverse computing for verification *)
    p := FLT(B); s := 0.0;
    FOR i := 0 TO N-1 DO s := s + d[i]/p; p := p*B END;
    Texts.WriteString(W, " (");
    Texts.WriteRealFix(W, s, 0, 10);
    Texts.WriteString(W, ")");
    Texts.WriteLn(W)
  END
END Power

Q: I am learning the Python programming language A:

You can start with the official Python documentation, or use beginner friendly tutorials like W3Schools, GeeksforGeeks, YouTube, or paid courses.

I personally recommend learning from a structured course (YouTube or paid) and applying everything you learn by building small projects.

Whenever you get stuck, you can always refer back to the official documentation for deeper understanding.

Q: Reading file contents using with statement A:

Unless you specify a size, the read method reads the whole contents of the file.

From https://docs.python.org/2/library/stdtypes.html#file.read :

If the size argument is negative or omitted, read all data until EOF is reached.

Q: Why does 2e3 return 2000? Isn't 2 to the 3rd power equal to 8? A:

2e3 is scientific notation for 2000.0. It is the same as 2.0e03. Use the pow() function:

echo pow(2, 3); // 8
